Porting an existing NIS study to easyNIS

Source: vignettes/porting.Rmd
porting.Rmd

This short guide maps common steps in an existing NIS analysis to easyNIS. The code below runs on nis_example() data only. Its diagnosis and procedure slots are replaced with invented codes so the example does not reproduce a real study definition.

Replace regular-expression scans with prefix flags

For a regex such as ^A12.*|^B34.*, use the prefixes c("A12", "B34"). nis_flag_dx() checks each diagnosis slot on its own, so codes in adjacent slots cannot join into a false match. It ignores case, periods, and spaces. nis_flag_pr() does the same for procedure slots. position = "principal" checks slot 1; "secondary" checks diagnosis slots after slot 1; and "any" checks all available slots.

Prefix lists express literal starts only. A regex that requires a particular suffix or code length, uses a character class, or allows optional characters cannot be represented exactly. Keep that condition in a regular expression with a plain mutate()/if_any() expression on the code columns.

The example starts from generated data and substitutes illustrative codes, then creates diagnosis and procedure flags:

example_path <- nis_example(years = 2018:2020)

nis_flagged <- nis_open(example_path, years = 2018:2020) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    I10_DX1 = dplyr::if_else(AGE >= 50, "A1234", "C004"),
    I10_DX2 = dplyr::if_else(FEMALE == 1, "B34.1", "C00.5"),
    I10_PR1 = dplyr::if_else(FEMALE == 1, "0AB12", "0XY34")
  ) |>
  nis_flag_dx(cohort_dx = c("A12", "B34"), position = "principal") |>
  nis_flag_dx(exposure = "B34", position = "any") |>
  nis_flag_pr(example_procedure = "0AB", position = "any")
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:

#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.

For a regex that needs a suffix test, keep the expression explicit. For example, this checks for an invented code with exactly two digits after A12 in any diagnosis slot:

nis_flagged <- nis_flagged |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    exact_code = dplyr::coalesce(
      dplyr::if_any(
        dplyr::starts_with("I10_DX"),
        ~ grepl("^A12[0-9]{2}$", as.character(.x))
      ),
      FALSE
    )
  )

The prefix and regex paths serve different definitions: use the simpler prefix flag where the condition is a literal prefix, and retain the regex where the suffix matters.

Replace local recode helpers

If a local cleaning helper used case_when() to turn known HCUP codes such as sex, payer, or discharge disposition into labels, remove those repeated recodes. nis_design() calls nis_label() on the collected analysis data. Known value codes become factors and receive variable labels; unknown values are not given guessed labels. You can call nis_label() directly on a collected data frame when you need the same recoding outside nis_design().

Keep custom study-derived variables in mutate(). Set their factor order explicitly with forcats::fct_relevel(), and override the displayed label at the table where it is used:

study_design <- nis_flagged |>
  nis_design(
    cohort = cohort_dx & AGE >= 50,
    keep = c(
      AGE, FEMALE, DIED, LOS, TOTCHG, CCR_NIS,
      cohort_dx, exposure, example_procedure
    ),
    dollars = 2020
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    exposed = forcats::fct_relevel(
      factor(
        dplyr::if_else(as.character(exposure) == "Yes", "Yes", "No"),
        levels = c("No", "Yes")
      ),
      "No"
    ),
    age_band = forcats::fct_relevel(
      factor(dplyr::if_else(AGE >= 65, "65 or older", "Under 65")),
      "Under 65"
    )
  )
#> Warning: Missing values are always removed in SQL aggregation functions.
#> Use `na.rm = TRUE` to silence this warning
#> This warning is displayed once every 8 hours.
#> Cohort: 201 discharges; weighted N 239.7; 36 hospitals across 3 years.

Use gtsummary label overrides for derived variables; HCUP labels already cover the common coded fields:

table_one <- gtsummary::tbl_svysummary(
  study_design,
  by = exposed,
  include = c(AGE, FEMALE, age_band, DIED, LOS, cost_adj),
  label = list(
    age_band ~ "Illustrative age group",
    cost_adj ~ "Hospital cost in 2020 USD"
  )
)

table_one$table_body |>
  dplyr::select(variable, label) |>
  dplyr::distinct()
#> # A tibble: 10 × 2
#>    variable label                      
#>    <chr>    <chr>                      
#>  1 AGE      Age, years                 
#>  2 FEMALE   Sex of patient             
#>  3 FEMALE   Male                       
#>  4 FEMALE   Female                     
#>  5 age_band Illustrative age group     
#>  6 age_band Under 65                   
#>  7 age_band 65 or older                
#>  8 DIED     Died during hospitalization
#>  9 LOS      Length of stay, days       
#> 10 cost_adj Hospital cost in 2020 USD

Declare the cohort with nis_design()

Older scripts may build survey::svydesign() with HOSPID and TRENDWT, then call subset() for the analysis cohort. Those fields are not available in current NIS releases. For the supported ICD-10 years, nis_design() uses HOSP_NIS, NIS_STRATUM, and DISCWT, and makes hospital and stratum IDs year-specific before combining years. Pass the cohort expression and the columns to retain; do not filter to the cohort before constructing the design.

The design retains one placeholder for each hospital-year with no cohort discharges. This lets the survey domain retain the sampled hospital context when estimating the declared cohort. The placeholder-row method is experimental and should be validated against a full-data design for the analysis at hand. After nis_design(), filters should only narrow the cohort declared by its cohort argument.

Replace charge adjustment and testing switches

If adj_TOTCHG was inflation-adjusted charges, its counterpart is charges_adj. cost_adj estimates hospital cost by multiplying charges by CCR_NIS before inflation adjustment. With TOTCHG and CCR_NIS in keep, nis_design(..., dollars = 2020) creates both fields, as in the example above. For a collected data frame, call nis_cost(data, dollars = 2020) directly.

Replace a TESTING switch that points to a small hand-picked data file with nis_example(years = 2018:2020). It writes an invented, temporary dataset with the same broad column shape needed to run the pipeline; it contains no study records.

The example directory can be removed after use with unlink(example_path, recursive = TRUE).

Common pitfalls

Common pitfalls

  • Regex expressions may encode suffix rules that a prefix flag cannot reproduce. Review each code-set translation.
  • A pooled analysis needs year-scoped hospital and stratum identifiers and a stated weight convention.
  • Never treat nis_example() results as study or national estimates.

Function references: nis_open(), nis_flag_dx(), nis_flag_pr(), nis_design(), nis_cost(), and nis_suppress().
